chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from one of them both عليهما السلام, who said:

If the traveler does not find water, then let him refrain as long as he remains within the time. Then when he fears that it will pass him by, let him perform tayammum and pray at the end of the time. Then if he finds water, there is no qaḍāʾ upon him, and let him perform wudu (ablution) for what he will face next.

key_terms.آخِرِ الْوَقْتِ: the end portion of the prayer time
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرُ: the traveler who is subject to this ruling
key_terms.فَلَا قَضَاءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no repeat performance due upon him
key_terms.فَلْيَتَيَمَّمْ: let him perform tayammum as a substitute purification
key_terms.وَلْيَتَوَضَّأْ: let him perform wudu (ablution) afterward for upcoming prayers

ai.seo_question: What should a traveler do if no water is available before the time of prayer ends?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a traveler who cannot find water during the time of salat (prayer). He should delay the prayer while hoping to find water, then perform tayammum near the end of the prayer time if he fears the time will expire, and if he later finds water he does not repeat that prayer.
